blockers.quote: His coffee's gone. His rent doubles. He's the pickpocket now. To everyone but you.
blockers.why: #22 A laugh in every scene fails. From the coffee refusal through the platform isolation and bias diagrams, several consecutive scenes are sad, and the sequence runs well over twenty seconds.
blockers.fix: Compress lines 347–375 into one comic escalation under twenty seconds: the seller repeatedly pulls the cup away as his tag predicts each reach, the landlord swaps in the full-rent envelope, and commuters sidestep him so far that they crowd beside the pickpocket. Keep the coffee-on-the-crate scene as the sole tender beat.

blockers.quote: The kid with the cap plays rock-paper-scissors for the seat by the door. Wins with rock. His tag says rock again.
blockers.why: #20 Escalating set pieces fails. A children's game follows the pickpocket's citywide social verdict, making the next use smaller than the last.
blockers.fix: Reorder this run as kid, magician, pickpocket, televised football, then the forty-phone train, so each use expands from a game to a livelihood, public exclusion, citywide entertainment and finally the whole population.

blockers.quote: Across the aisle, the kid with the cap. No phone. Over his head, a card with nothing on it. He winks.
blockers.why: #11 Never say the feeling fails because the narration repeats every element already visible in the preceding scene direction, weakening the final image.
blockers.fix: Delete this line and replace line 547 with: "And the city hasn't noticed yet."

suggestions.quote: Pocket the key, and the city's right, and your rent stays half. Hold it out, and your tag goes crimson in front of everyone. And so, maybe, does your money.
suggestions.fix: Sharpen the two-right-answers dilemma: "Pocket the key, and your rent stays half—but his tag becomes the truth. Hold it out, and both rents in that box depend on what he does next."

suggestions.quote: A hundred and sixty teams once tried to predict how children's lives would turn out (c24). Thousands of facts on every family (c24). The best guesses were only slightly better than a simple one from four facts (c24).
suggestions.fix: Cut this post-peak study and move directly from the board reaching seventy-one to "It never got better at seeing you."

suggestions.quote: So, would you pay full price to make your card go blank? Tell us in the comments. And if you would, hit like and subscribe.
suggestions.fix: Keep only: "Would you pay full price to make your card go blank?" Let the silent end card carry the like-and-subscribe request.

keep.quote: You've put that key in your pocket a thousand times. Tonight it's the first time you've locked something away from him.
You can't steal what you've just been handed. And the machine had no card for that.
It never got better at seeing you. You got better at being seen.
